page: OVHcloud h100-760 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9354 processor under KVM virtualization. The architecture provides 60 physical cores and 60 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 760 GB of system RAM, offering 12.67 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs delivering a combined 160 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM. Local high-speed storage is integrated with a 7,880 GB NVMe SSD array, complemented by a baseline network throughput of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight significant compute and inference capabilities. In LLM inference tests, the dual H100 configuration achieves 727.7 tokens per second prompt processing and 29.48 tokens per second text generation on a 70B parameter model, alongside 4,587.57 prompt tokens per second on a 7B model. CPU synthetic workloads match this high tier, registering 156,986.02 in stress-ng multi-core execution and 93,218.13 in PassMark CPU testing. In-memory data structures perform strongly, with Redis SET throughput reaching 132.44 million operations per second, supported by 8,491.57 GB/s cached read memory bandwidth.

The hardware configuration provides high density by pairing enterprise accelerators with expansive local NVMe capacity and a high memory-to-core ratio. While uncached large-block system memory operations and static web throughput operate in intermediate performance bands, computational density remains prioritized. These characteristics make the instance suitable for large language model serving, distributed deep learning training, massive vectorized database processing, and data-intensive scientific simulations.
description: OVHcloud h100-760 is a high-density GPU-accelerated cloud instance engineered for computationally intensive AI and scientific workloads. Powered by a 60-core AMD EPYC 9354 processor running at 3.0 GHz without multithreading, the system includes 760 GB of system memory, yielding 12.67 GB per dedicated core. Hardware acceleration is provided by two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs with 160 GB of total VRAM, paired with 7,880 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show top-decile performance across multi-core CPU metrics, Redis operations at 132.44 million ops/sec, and LLM inference speeds reaching 727.7 prompt tokens per second on 70B models. While uncached memory throughput operates at moderate levels, the paired GPU and NVMe resources deliver strong resource efficiency for deep learning inference, model fine-tuning, and high-throughput vector processing.
